from.place: Pointwise component reduction of the proper base-change proof

source.place: proper base change proof, componentwise reduction

proof.text: Choose a bounded constructible integral model M of the continuous E exchange at K, retaining the actual Arrow isomorphism with its E scalar extension.

The integral exchange at M becomes invertible after residue reduction by proper torsion base change. The scheme Y′ is noetherian because it is of finite type over a field, so integral reduction conservativity makes the integral exchange itself invertible.

Derived E scalar extension preserves isomorphisms. Transport invertibility through the Arrow isomorphism of step 1 and reflect it from the ambient full subcategory morphism to the bounded constructible morphism.

title: Pointwise proper base change for condensed finite coefficient
statement: For the prime, finite normed extension, field, separated finite-type corners, morphisms over the field, cartesian square and proper f of the proper base-change target, every object K in the source bounded constructible condensed E category has an invertible component of the specified boundedConstructibleBaseChange natural transformation.
